text: What is the central theme of Jack Finney's 'The Third Level'?
options: The power of imagination
The importance of technology
The danger of time travel
The value of friendship
explanation: The story revolves around a man who discovers a mysterious train that takes him to different levels of time. The central theme is the power of imagination, which allows him to experience different eras and realities.

options: The tiger king himself
A journalist
A hunter
A conservationist

text: What is the significance of the journey to the end of the Earth in Tishani Doshi's poem?
options: It represents a physical journey to the end of the world
It symbolizes a spiritual journey to self-discovery
It represents a metaphorical journey through time
It is a literal journey to a physical location
correctAnswer: It symbolizes a spiritual journey to self-discovery
explanation: The poem describes a journey to the end of the Earth, but it is not a physical journey. Instead, it represents a spiritual journey to self-discovery, where the speaker reflects on their own identity and the world around them.

text: What is the main conflict in Pearl S. Buck's 'The Enemy'?
options: The conflict between good and evil
The conflict between tradition and modernity
The conflict between the individual and society
The conflict between love and hate
correctAnswer: The conflict between the individual and society
explanation: The story revolves around a young woman who struggles with her own identity and the expectations of her society. The main conflict is between the individual and society, as she tries to navigate her own desires and aspirations within the constraints of her culture.

text: What is the tone of Susan Hill's 'On the Face of It'?
options: Serious and somber
Humorous and lighthearted
Mysterious and suspenseful
Reflective and introspective
explanation: The story has a mysterious and suspenseful tone, as the narrator tries to unravel the mystery of a strange occurrence. The tone is tense and intriguing, keeping the reader engaged and curious.

text: What is the significance of the title 'Memories of Childhood' in Zitkala-Sa's and Bama's essays?
options: It represents a nostalgic look back at childhood
It symbolizes a journey through time to the past
It represents a reflection on the experiences of childhood
It is a literal title with no deeper meaning
correctAnswer: It represents a reflection on the experiences of childhood
explanation: The title 'Memories of Childhood' represents a reflection on the experiences of childhood, as the authors look back on their own childhood memories and experiences. The title is significant because it highlights the importance of childhood experiences in shaping our identities and perspectives.
